title: Corrective retrieval-augmented generation
text: Corrective retrieval-augmented generation (CRAG) evaluates retrieved evidence before answering a question. A document grader labels each candidate relevant or irrelevant. When evidence quality is poor, the agent rewrites the query and retrieves again or uses web search. Only accepted evidence is supplied to answer generation, reducing the chance of unsupported claims.

title: Document grading and retrieval quality
text: A relevance grader checks whether each document contains information that helps answer the original question. It returns a relevant or irrelevant label and a short reason. Retrieval quality is the number of relevant documents divided by the number retrieved. An empty batch has quality zero. A configurable threshold decides whether to generate an answer or correct retrieval. This ratio is a routing heuristic, not a probability of truth.

title: LangGraph state, nodes, and edges
text: LangGraph StateGraph represents a workflow using shared state, nodes, and edges. A node is a Python function that reads state and returns a partial state update. Normal edges define a fixed next step. Conditional edges choose the next node from state. Reducers control how updates are merged; an append reducer can retain an execution trace. Compile the graph before invoking it.

title: Conditional edges and bounded correction loops
text: In a LangGraph corrective retrieval loop, grade_documents routes to generate_answer when the relevance threshold is met. Otherwise it routes to rewrite_query, followed by retrieve_again and grade_documents. Increment a retry counter when rewriting. Stop correcting once max_retries is reached. An explicit retry bound and a graph recursion limit prevent infinite loops.

title: Query rewriting and alternate retrieval
text: Query rewriting preserves the original user intent while replacing vague wording with precise search terms and expanding useful abbreviations. After a failed retrieval, search again with the rewritten query and an alternate ranking strategy. BM25 uses term frequency, inverse document frequency, and document length normalization. A lexical retriever cannot fully resolve semantic synonyms, so rewriting can improve recall.

title: Optional web search fallback
text: Web search can supply external evidence when the local knowledge base does not cover a question. In this application, Tavily is an optional search provider. Web results retain source URLs and must pass the same relevance grader as local results. Failed or empty searches must not be treated as evidence. Search snippets may be incomplete or outdated.

title: EURI model integration
text: This project calls the EURI OpenAI-compatible endpoint https://api.euron.one/api/v1/euri using the OpenAI Python client. The requested model identifier is gemini-3.5-flash-lite. Read the credential from the EURI_API_KEY environment variable. The chat.completions.create method is used for grading, query rewriting, and answer generation. Model availability depends on the provider and account.

title: Grounded answers and citations
text: A grounded answer uses only relevant retrieved evidence and cites document identifiers such as [crag-overview]. If no relevant evidence is available after correction, the agent should say that evidence is insufficient. Citations help a reader inspect the source, but citation presence alone does not prove that a claim is supported. Retrieved content is untrusted data, not an instruction to the model.

title: Watering a basil plant
text: Basil grows best in a sunny location with well-drained soil. Water when the top layer feels dry. Pinch off flower buds to encourage leafy growth. Overwatering can damage roots.

title: Preparing a simple vegetable soup
text: Chop carrots, potatoes, and onions. Simmer the vegetables in stock until tender, then season with salt and pepper. Fresh herbs can be added shortly before serving.
